newsitem.title: USA: New York Bagel off on Q4 EPS outlook.
newsitem.headline: New York Bagel off on Q4 EPS outlook.

text.p: New York Bagel Enterprises Inc shares dropped 2-3/8 to 4-3/8 on Monday, after the company announced a fourth quarter earnings projection that was lower than analysts had been expecting, a spokesman said.
Earlier, the company said it expects earnings for the fourth quarter of $0.04 to $0.05 a share, up from pro forma year-ago earnings of $0.02 a share.
"The analysts were looking for a stronger number. I think they were reading in the $0.07 to $0.08 range," Paul Hoover, vice president, strategic planning, said.
Revenues for the quarter rose to $3.3 million from $2.0 million.

The company said higher percentage labor costs and higher depreciation and amortization expenses from new restaurant openings and the Lots A' Bagels acquisition, completed in December, tempered earnings growth in the quarter.
"I do look at them as short-term costs," Hoover said.
New York Bagel grew to 33 bagel restaurants at year-end 1996 from 15 at year-end 1995, with 10 units acquired or built in the fourth quarter alone, he added.

New York Bagel also said its weighted average shares outstanding in the fourth quarter also rose to 4,686,024 compared with 3,018,538 in the fourth quarter of 1995 due to an initial public offering in August 1996.
